We need to propose a retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves must be commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to construct JSON with reactions and molecules.

Target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Looks like a sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings, one with para-methyl, other with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So we can think disconnections:

1) Disconnection of sulfonamide: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline. Use sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl) + aniline (the first phenyl with methyl). So step 1: sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl) + aniline (para-methyl phenyl amine) -> target via sulfonamide formation.

2) The aryl sulfonyl chloride could be made from the corresponding aryl sulfonic acid (or from chlorosulfonation of bromobenzene). But we can buy the sulfonyl chloride directly if commercially available. Let's check if ClSO2-aryl with methyl substituent is available: e.g., 4-methylbenzenesulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride, TsCl). That's a common reagent, cheap. Its SMILES: "CS(=O)(=O)Cl". Actually p-toluenesulfonyl chloride is "Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1". That's exactly the left phenyl with methyl and sulfonyl chloride. Good.

So step 1: React p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) with the other aryl amine (the second phenyl with the unsaturated amide). The amine is "c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2" (para-substituted phenyl with the side chain). That amine is an aniline (para-aminophenyl) attached to the side chain. So we need that amine as a leaf.

Thus leaf 1: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (commercial, cheap). Leaf 2: 4-(E-((E)-2-((4-aminophenyl)carbamoyl)phenyl)vinyl)aniline? Actually the amine is "c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2" which is a phenyl with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline. The amine is the para position of that phenyl (the phenyl is attached to sulfonyl group via N). Wait the sulfonamide attaches to the left phenyl (p-tolyl) via N to sulfonyl group, and the right phenyl is attached to sulfonyl group via the sulfonyl group (the sulfonyl attached to the right phenyl as aryl sulfone). Actually the SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Interpretation: p-tolyl (Cc1ccc(... )cc1) attached via N to sulfonyl group: NS(=O)(=O) attached to second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the p-tolyl ring (aniline). The sulfonyl group attached to the second phenyl (aryl sulfone). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of the p-tolyl aniline (p-toluidine). So we need p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) as the amine, reacting with aryl sulfonyl chloride (the sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl). Wait typical sulfonamide formation: aryl sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide. So we need aryl sulfonyl chloride where the aryl is the second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2). So we need "4-(E-((E)-2-((4-aminophenyl)carbamoyl)phenyl)vinyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride". That's not commercially available likely. So maybe better to reverse: use p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) + the second phenyl amine (which is an aniline). That would give sulfonamide where the nitrogen is attached to the second phenyl, not the first. But our target has nitrogen attached to the first phenyl (p-tolyl). So we need the sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl, not TsCl.

Alternative: Use sulfonylation of p-toluidine with aryl sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl. Could we make that aryl sulfonyl chloride via chlorosulfonation of the second phenyl (which has the side chain). That could be a step: start from the second phenyl (the aryl with side chain) as a sulfonic acid (or sulfonyl chloride). But maybe we can use a different disconnection: break the C=C double bond (retro-aldol) to give an aldehyde and amide? Or break the amide to give an acid and aniline.

Simplify: Use two steps: 1) Form the amide via coupling of aniline (c3ccccc3N) with acrylic acid derivative? Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl. That's an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we can make that via condensation of aniline with acryloyl chloride? Wait the amide is attached to the unsaturated chain: C= C - C(=O)N-aryl. So we could start from aniline (aniline) and acryloyl chloride to give N-phenylacrylamide (c3ccccc3N-CO-CH=CH2). Then do a Heck coupling to attach the phenyl ring (the second phenyl) at the β position? Actually the unsaturated amide is attached to the phenyl ring via the double bond: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-N-phenyl. That's a trans-stilbene type with amide at one end. Could be formed via Heck coupling of an aryl bromide with acrylamide. So we could have aryl bromide (the second phenyl bromide) + N-phenylacrylamide -> product.

Thus route: Step A: Synthesize N-phenylacrylamide (C=CC(=O)Nc1ccccc1). This is commercially available? Search earlier gave "NC(=O)C=CC1=CC=C(N)C=C1" which is N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide? Actually that SMILES is "NC(=O)C=CC1=CC=C(N)C=C1" which is an aniline attached to the phenyl ring, not the amide nitrogen. Wait we need N-phenylacrylamide (acrylamide attached to phenyl). That's "C=CC(=O)Nc1ccccc1". Search gave that as "NC1=CC=CC=C1NC(=O)C=C" which is anilide with extra aniline? Not correct. Let's search for "C=CC(=O)Nc1ccccc1". Already did, got price 522. That's the correct compound: N-phenylacrylamide (also called cinnamamide). Good.

So leaf 1: N-phenylacrylamide (C=CC(=O)Nc1ccccc1) price 522.

Step 2: Heck coupling of N-phenylacrylamide with 4-bromo-? The second phenyl is "c2ccc(... )cc2" where the substituent is the unsaturated amide at para position? Actually the SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. This is a phenyl ring with the unsaturated amide attached at para position (maybe). So we need a bromophenyl (4-bromo phenyl) to couple with the acrylamide to give the trans product. So leaf 2: 4-bromo-? The phenyl also has no other substituents. So 4-bromo phenyl (bromobenzene) is cheap. But we need the final product after Heck: the phenyl with the unsaturated amide attached. So we can use 4-bromobenzene (bromobenzene) as starting material, Heck with N-phenylacrylamide to give trans-4-(cinnamoyl)aniline? Wait the product would be 4-(cinnamoyl)aniline? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N) which is the aniline part of the amide. In our target, the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl (c3ccccc3N) which is separate from the phenyl bearing the double bond. So the unsaturated amide is attached to the phenyl via the carbonyl carbon, not via nitrogen. So the product of Heck between 4-bromo phenyl and N-phenylacrylamide would give 4-(cinnamoyl)aniline? Wait N-phenylacrylamide has the phenyl attached to the nitrogen, not the carbonyl. So coupling at the double bond would give a phenyl attached to the β-carbon, resulting in a structure where the phenyl (from bromobenzene) is attached to the double bond, and the amide nitrogen still attached to its phenyl. That matches our target: phenyl (c2) attached to the double bond, which is attached to carbonyl attached to aniline (c3). Yes.

Thus step 2: Heck coupling of 4-bromobenzene with N-phenylacrylamide to give 4-(E-((E)-2-((4-aminophenyl)carbamoyl)phenyl)vinyl)aniline? Wait the product would be 4-(E-2-((phenyl)carbamoyl)vinyl)aniline? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3). So product is 4-(E-2-(phenylcarbamoyl)vinyl)aniline. That's exactly the second phenyl with side chain.

So leaf 2: 4-bromobenzene (or 4-bromo-? Actually we need para position for coupling, but bromobenzene is unsubstituted; after coupling, the bromine is replaced, giving phenyl with the side chain at para? Wait bromobenzene has bromine at one position; after Heck, the bromine is replaced by the alkene, giving phenyl with the side chain at that position (the position where bromine was). So product is phenyl with side chain at that position, which is para relative to nothing else. That's fine.

Thus step 2 yields the aryl sulfonyl chloride? No, yields the aryl amine (the second phenyl with side chain) which still has an aniline (the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl). Actually the product after Heck still has the aniline (the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl). The amine we need for sulfonamide formation is the p-toluidine (the left phenyl). Wait the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to p-tolyl, not the second phenyl. So we need p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) as the amine for sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl. But we are forming the second phenyl sulfonyl chloride later.

Alternative route: Use sulfonylation of p-toluidine with aryl sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl. So we need aryl sulfonyl chloride (the second phenyl with side chain). That could be made from the aryl sulfonic acid via chlorination. So step 3: Convert the aryl sulfonic acid (or sulfonate) to sulfonyl chloride using SOCl2. So we need the aryl sulfonic acid (the second phenyl with side chain and sulfonic acid group). That could be obtained by sulfonation of the second phenyl (the one we made via Heck) using chlorosulfonic acid (ClSO3H) to install -SO3H at para position? But the phenyl already has the side chain at para; we need sulfonyl group attached to that phenyl (the one we made) at the position where we will later attach to p-toluidine via sulfonamide. In target, the sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl at para position relative to the side chain? Let's examine SMILES: ...NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2. The sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl at the position ortho to the side chain? Actually the SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2. The sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl via S attached to the phenyl carbon (c2). The phenyl has two substituents: the sulfonyl group (attached to the carbon bearing the N) and the side chain (the unsaturated amide) attached at another carbon. The order in SMILES suggests the sulfonyl group is at position 1, side chain at position 4 (para). So the phenyl is disubstituted para to each other. So we need to install sulfonyl group at one position and the side chain at para.

Thus we could start from 4-bromo-1-chlorobenzene? Actually we need a phenyl with two substituents: one is sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and the other is the side chain. Could we start from 4-bromo-1-chlorobenzene? Not straightforward.

Alternative route: Use sulfonylation first, then Heck. Start with p-toluidine (aniline) and p-toluenesulfonyl chloride? That gives sulfonamide where sulfonyl is p-tolyl, not correct.

Maybe better to reverse: Use sulfonyl chloride derived from p-tolyl (TsCl) and the second phenyl amine (the aniline). That would give sulfonamide where the nitrogen is attached to the second phenyl (the aniline). But our target has nitrogen attached to p-tolyl. Could we simply invert the naming? The SMILES shows NS(=O)(=O)c2... The N is attached to the left phenyl (p-tolyl). So we need p-toluidine as the nucleophile. So we need sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl.

Thus we need to synthesize aryl sulfonyl chloride (aryl = phenyl with side chain). This can be made by chlorosulfonation of the phenyl with side chain (the product of Heck). So step 2: Heck to give phenyl with side chain (no sulfonyl). Step 3: Chlorosulfonation (ClSO3H) to install -SO3H at the position ortho to side chain? But we need para to side chain. The phenyl currently has side chain at para position (if we used 4-bromo phenyl). After chlorosulfonation, the sulfonic acid will go to the ortho or para positions; but para is already occupied, so it will go to ortho. In target, sulfonyl is ortho to side chain? Let's check: In SMILES, c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2, the sulfonyl attached to c2 (the first carbon after NS(=O)(=O)). The side chain is after c2ccc(... )cc2, meaning the side chain is at position 4 relative to the sulfonyl? Actually the pattern: c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2 means the phenyl has a substituent at position 4 (the /C=C...). The sulfonyl is attached to the phenyl at the position where the N attaches (the first carbon). So they are para to each other. So sulfonyl at position 1, side chain at position 4 (para). So we need sulfonyl at position 1, side chain at para. Starting from 4-bromo phenyl, after Heck we have side chain at position 4 (since bromine at position 1 replaced). So we have phenyl with side chain at para, and a hydrogen at position 1 (where bromine was). We need to convert that hydrogen to sulfonyl chloride. That can be done via chlorosulfonation (ClSO3H) which typically adds sulfonic acid at the para position relative to existing substituents, but if para is occupied, it may go ortho. However, chlorosulfonation of bromobenzene derivatives often gives sulfonic acid at the para position relative to bromine (which is now side chain). Since para is occupied, it may give ortho. Not ideal.

Alternative: Use a different order: first sulfonylate a phenyl (e.g., chlorosulfonate of bromobenzene) to give sulfonyl chloride at position 1, then perform Heck at the bromine position (which is ortho to sulfonyl). That would give sulfonyl at position 1, side chain at ortho, not para. Not match.

Maybe we can use a different starting phenyl: start from 4-bromo-1-chlorobenzene? Not.

Given time, maybe we can propose a 2-step route using commercially available sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) and commercially available aniline with side chain (the second phenyl with side chain and an amine). Wait is there a commercially available "4-(E-((E)-2-((4-aminophenyl)carbamoyl)phenyl)vinyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride"? Probably not.

But we could propose a 3-step route: 1) Synthesize the side-chain phenyl amine (the second phenyl) via Heck as described. 2) Sulfonylate that phenyl amine with chlorosulfonic acid to give sulfonyl chloride attached to the phenyl (but that would be on the same ring as the amine, not correct). Actually we need sulfonyl attached to the phenyl, not the amine. The sulfonyl is attached to the phenyl carbon, not to nitrogen. So we need to install sulfonyl group onto the phenyl ring (the same ring that already has side chain). That can be done via sulfonyl chloride formation from sulfonic acid (via chlorination). So step 2: chlorosulfonation of the phenyl (with side chain) to give sulfonic acid at ortho position (maybe). Then convert to sulfonyl chloride. Then step 3: couple with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide.

Thus leaves: p-toluidine (commercial cheap), 4-bromobenzene (commercial), N-phenylacrylamide (commercial). Also chlorosulfonic acid (ClSO3H) is reagent, not leaf. The sulfonic acid intermediate not needed as leaf.

We need to ensure total price <= 9999. Prices: p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) price 28.6 (or 115). 4-bromobenzene price? Not searched yet. Let's search.
